facts.raw_span: A 75-year-old woman
presumed stroke in April 2020
slurred speech, imbalance, and confusion lasting 48 hours
brain MRI showed chronic periventricular white matter changes without acute ischemic lesions
CT angiography demonstrated carotid tortuosity with stenosis from myointimal plaques
barnidipine 20 mg daily, clopidogrel 75 mg daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg daily
recurrent dizzying attacks characterized by sudden subjective vertigo, absence of nausea or vomiting, and unsteadiness with a wide-based gait requiring support
general and neurologic examinations were normal
severe dizziness worsened by any movement or position change, without nausea or vomiting
Romberg’s test was positive, with marked unsteadiness on eye closure
The HINTS examination was negative
Transcranial Doppler confirmed tortuosity and plaques but demonstrated normal hemodynamics of the cerebro-afferent vessels
